technical_and_design_decisions: Use Apache Geode / Pivotal GemFire Java client libraries compatible with Java 17+ and Spring Framework standards.
Implement the Spring Cloud Stream GemFire binder using GemFire ClientCache, Region-based data structures, and Continuous Queries (CQ) / CacheListeners for event messaging.
Persist Stream Definitions and Module Registries within dedicated, replicated or partitioned GemFire Regions to ensure high availability.
Extend the Spring Cloud Data Flow DSL parser and Shell commands to recognize stream tap destination syntax (e.g., `:streamname.module > sink`).
Structure documentation using AsciiDoc within the project repository to detail deployment manifests, partitioning configuration, and direct binding CLI usages.
assumptions: A local or containerized Pivotal GemFire / Apache Geode environment is available for development and integration testing.
The target infrastructure follows the modular Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) and Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) architectural patterns.
The software developer possesses prior experience with Java, Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow internals, and Apache Geode/GemFire APIs.
User story U5's truncated description ('I'd like to understand how streams withe') refers to stream partitioning mechanisms in deployment manifests.

activities.activity_description: Analyze requirements U1-U8, define SPI interfaces for GemFire deployment, design message channel binder architecture, and draft DSL extensions for pipeline tapping.
Implement Spring Cloud Stream GemFire binder, including inbound/outbound channel adapters, region provisioning, header mapping, auto-configuration, and unit tests.
Implement the Spring Cloud Data Flow Deployer SPI for GemFire, enabling orchestrating, launching, and managing data microservice lifecycles on GemFire infrastructure.
Develop StreamDefinition repository implementation backed by GemFire regions, providing CRUD operations and query support for stream pipelines.
Develop ModuleRegistry implementation backed by GemFire, allowing stream module artifacts and metadata to be registered and retrieved across the cluster.
Implement runtime support to non-destructively tap into primary pipeline channels and redirect copied event streams to secondary destinations for ad-hoc analysis.
Enhance the Data Flow DSL grammar, parser, and Shell interactive CLI to support tap creation, listing, and lifecycle management syntax.
Write detailed reference documentation covering deployment manifest partitioning properties (U5) and direct binding module launcher usage examples (U6).
Develop end-to-end integration tests using an embedded/containerized GemFire cluster to validate pipeline creation, tapping, direct binding, and binder performance.
